Instead, using a variant of our machinery we give a closely related application to distance amplification for locally testable codes with near-optimal distance-alphabet trade-off. The resulting codes are list-decodable and preserve testability up to a log factor in the alphabet. F. Further Applications Finally, we discuss our applications of Theorem II.1 and Theorem II.5 beyond agreement testing. a) Geometric Overlap.: A complex X has (d, c)geometric overlap if for every embedding X (1) into Rd−1 , there is a point q ∈ Rd−1 that lies in the convex hulls of at least a c-fraction of X’s embedded d-faces. [48] proved every d-uniform bounded degree complex has geometric overlap at best cd , where cd is the overlap of the complete complex. We prove sufficiently strong high dimensional expanders match this bound.
